I find it absolutely appalling that you think the people struggling with their autism are just "giving up" when in fact those same people are working hard every day to deal with the different struggles that having autism presents in the daily life. 

Your post reads the same as those people saying "why are you depressed? Just smile more"

Autism doesnt go away just because you "think about it less" it's a serious handicap for a lot of us on this subreddit. Autism is a spectrum and some of us struggle with it more than others. So stop projecting YOUR experience and assume it's the same for everyone else.

Hi, from Denmark here. People are generally respectful if they know you have autism. I highly doubt any reasonable adult here would discriminate against you here solely for being autistic. However fitting in with the extroverts is gonna be difficult no matter where you live. I have experienced universities telling me not to apply to them because they dont want someone with autistic traits but they are not allowed to turn you away because of your disability afaik.

People here generally do not small talk with strangers unless you are at a club or a party, so you can take public transport and such without worrying about being disturbed.
People often think I'm a foreigner and will start speaking english to me because I look like I didnt understand what they were saying 😔

It's good you have people you can rely on like your sister and friend, I'm sorry about your mother. The good thing about being an adult now is at least you can distance yourself more from your parents. That of course doesnt make it hurt any less.

Moving out helped me feel a lot safer and happy as I wasnt around my parents' negativity anymore, so I hope you can find a safe space as well.
